What else matters besides price per Wh?

Battery chemistry: Prefer LiFePO4, typically rated for thousands of cycles.

Inverter output: A 2,000 Wh battery with a 500 W inverter cannot run a 1,500 W appliance.

Solar input: Higher solar charging wattage can make a big difference when using panels.

Usable capacity: AC conversion losses mean you might only get 80–90% of the advertised Wh.

Warranty: Look for a reputable manufacturer offering 3–5 years of coverage.

My target purchase price would be $0.35/Wh or less for a 2 kWh unit. Below $0.25/Wh would be unusually attractive, provided the brand, warranty, and specifications check out.

One important distinction: a solar generator often doesn't include solar panels. If panels are included, evaluate their value separately.

Are you looking at a 1,000 Wh, 2,000 Wh, or 3,000+ Wh generator? The ideal price per Wh changes somewhat with capacity.
markup:
For a portable solar generator (also called a portable power station), **$0.30–$0.50 per watt-hour (Wh) is a good price**, assuming you're buying a reputable brand with a LiFePO4 (LFP) battery.

## Price per Wh benchmarks

| Price per Wh | Value |
|---|---|
| Under $0.25 | <badge color="success">Exceptional deal</badge> |
| $0.25–$0.35 | Excellent |
| $0.35–$0.50 | Good |
| $0.50–$0.70 | Fair |
| $0.70–$1.00 | Expensive |
| Over $1.00 | Poor value for most buyers |

These benchmarks apply primarily to power stations with approximately 1,000–3,000 Wh of battery capacity, without solar panels.

## How to calculate it

\[
\text{Price per Wh}=\frac{\text{Price in dollars}}{\text{Battery capacity in Wh}}
\]

For example, a 2,048 Wh power station selling for $699 costs:

\[
\$699 \div 2048 = \boxed{\$0.34/\text{Wh}}
\]

That would be an excellent price.

- **Battery chemistry:** Prefer LiFePO4, typically rated for thousands of cycles.

- **Usable capacity:** AC conversion losses mean you might only get 80–90% of the advertised Wh.

**My target purchase price would be $0.35/Wh or less for a 2 kWh unit.** Below $0.25/Wh would be unusually attractive, provided the brand, warranty, and specifications check out.
